$comment: The reset screen/locale screenshot matrix, re-cut by chunk 08 (design-system.md §15.3: 'The screenshot matrix is re-cut here'). Neither the historical 0/32 nor the 32 images observed on 2026-09-08 carries forward -- both describe the Hajj screen set. Chunk 27 enforces completeness as a release gate; this file is what it enforces against. reset-matrix.test.ts keeps every claim here honest against the matrix actually derived from the Maestro flows.

implemented.$comment: Captured today. Each name is the Maestro `takeScreenshot` basename without its locale suffix, and each must exist in the derived matrix for both locales on every platform the group declares. `platforms` is required: two eSIM activation screens exist on one platform only, and declaring them for both would make the other platform's matrix permanently and misleadingly incomplete.

designSystem.why: The design system's own evidence. Product screens for the reset are not built yet, and capturing half-built versions would produce a matrix to throw away the moment chunks 18-24 land. These prove what those screens would otherwise each get wrong separately: the tint rule, French expansion, no state carried by colour alone, and a stale reading that still says how stale it is.

retained.why: Screens that still ship. Their coverage is retained rather than dropped: they are superseded by the reset journeys, not yet removed from the product, and deleting a flow for a screen a customer can still reach would lose real coverage to make a number look tidier.

retainedAndroidOnly.why: The single-tap activation prompt exists only on Android. Declaring it for both platforms would make the iOS matrix permanently, misleadingly incomplete.

retainedIosOnly.why: iOS has no single-tap path, so it gets the manual guide instead. Same reason as above, the other way round.

consumerNavigation.why: The new signed-out entry and the explicit no-service and load-error Home states required by chunk 18. Each state has a route out and is captured in both supported locales.

consumerPurchase.why: The purchase journey and, deliberately, its failures. A payment screen is mostly its error states, and the ones captured here are the states every deployment is actually in today: no live merchant account (D3/D4 open), an expired price, a declined payment, and a payment the processor has taken but not yet confirmed. Capturing only the happy path would evidence the one screen a customer is least likely to be stuck on.

consumerLine.why: My Line and the states it must never collapse. Three of the six exist because the schema keeps installation, activation and network attachment apart: a line installed and not yet switched on, a line suspended with the profile still on the phone, and a balance nobody has ever measured. The installation capture is deliberately the *unprotected* variant -- iOS cannot block a screenshot at all, so the warning copy is the whole mitigation and is the thing worth reviewing.

consumerCalls.why: US-47's internet-calling surface. Captured with `backgroundCall` reported as unavailable, which is the honest setting today and the one whose copy matters most: no adapter has proven that audio survives the app going to background, and the disclosure is the whole mitigation. The history capture includes a settled call, one still being metered and one nobody answered, because "no charge yet" and "no charge" must not look alike. V05's browser surface is the dashboard's matrix, not this one.

consumerAccount.why: The real account and receipt components with non-secret fixtures, rendered in both locales on both platforms.

pending.$comment: The mobile screen flows above are captured. These remaining reset surfaces live in the dashboard or internal operations, not in the mobile app; they require separate browser evidence before release. A screen may only move to `implemented` when its platform's harness actually captures it.

internalOperations.why: Visibly separate from any organization surface. §17.6 of design-system.md gives the rule; chunk 25 builds the screens.
